Guhyasamājatantra
Bud. (C. 300 A. D.) one of the earliest Buddhist tantras of the Vajrayāna school; originated in South India according to Tibetan traditions; in two parts; the Pūrvārdha in 18 Paṭalas is also called Aṣṭādaśapaṭala, the second part called Uttarārdha or Aparārdha is said to be spurious an. is in 15 Paṭalas; sometimes confused with the Mahāyāna text Tathāgataguhyasūtra. (See Winternitz, HIL. II, p. 392; IHQ. IX. i, p.. 1-2); but they are different. See L. M. Joshi, J. of Ori. Inst. M. S. Uni. Baroda XVI. p.. 138 ff.
Q. by Indrabhūti in his Jñānasiddhi an. by Advayavajra in his Advayavajrasaṅgraha. (See GOS. XLIV p.. 76-78; GOS. XL, p.. 49-50).
AMG. II. p. 299. AR. XX. p. 496. BBRAS. App. A. p. 493 (7). Br. Mus. 539. Cabaton I. 49-50. Cambr. Uni. Bud. p.. 15. 51 (both Pūrvārdha). 70 (Pūrvārdha an. Parārdha). 140 (Uttarārdha). Cordier III. p. 539. Hod. Bud. 44 (Uttarārdha, 15 Paṭalas). JBORS. XXI. i. p. 34 (inc.). XXIII. i. p. 49 (5 stray leaves). Kanjur Kyoto 81. Nanjio 1027. Nepal II. p.. 173-4 (Guhyasamādhi). 243-44 (Guhyātiguhyatantrarāja). RASB. I. 64. SBL. Nepal p.. 261-4.
Pt.. GOS. LIII. 1931.
